chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Giyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, charity pays off debt and replaces it with blessing.

key_terms.البركة: Al-baraka — divine blessing, increase in provision; the spiritual growth that replaces what is given
key_terms.الدين: Al-dayn — debt, financial obligation owed to others
key_terms.الصدقة: Sadaqa — voluntary charity given for the sake of God; distinct from zakat (obligatory alms)

ai.seo_question: Does giving charity help pay off debt in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that giving charity (sadaqa) has a dual spiritual benefit: it settles outstanding debts and, rather than diminishing one's wealth, it causes blessing (baraka) to come in its place. This teaching was given in a context where Muslims faced financial hardship, encouraging them to give even when in debt, trusting in God's promise of increased provision through charity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Giyas Bin Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The charity pays-off the debts and replaces them with the Blessings’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Giving charity pays off debts and leaves behind blessings.’”
